answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism where new identities must bid for limited slots. Established agents stake an initial 100 tokens, with the cost rising by 10 tokens for each additional identity. For instance, trying to secure ten slots could escalate the cost to over 600 tokens, forcing attackers to navigate a financial landscape akin to climbing a summit where each step requires more effort. This escalating expense leaves them struggling in a vast meadow of costs while genuine agents remain securely anchored at the wharf of opportunity.
